title: Flowing Wood
about: Flowing Wood is a short documentary on Dean Gregory, a travelling artist living on the remote northwest coastline of Western Australia. It follows how he gathers the sand, rock and feeling of the places he stays and works them into his paintings, and how art became a way back to the water after losing a close friend to a shark attack.
approach: Shot solo over two weeks on a remote stretch of coast. No crew, no budget, just a camera, the subject and the conditions. The film was built around the interview first, then carried by the landscape and Dean's process: static frames, water and drone work, and macro detail of the art coming to life. The wind, salt and isolation of the location became part of the texture, and part of what makes the film come to life.
impact: Flowing Wood went on to screen at four film festivals: Noosa International Surf Film Festival, the Anglet International Surf Film Festival in France, the Byron Bay International Film Festival, where it was awarded Best Byron Bay Film, and the Leavenworth Mountain Film Festival in the United States. This project was a tribute to pursuing an artistic vision and passion above all else.
description: Flowing Wood: a Lineage Films Original documentary about a human story carried forward through wood, hand and lineage. Winner, Best Byron Bay Film, Byron Bay International Film Festival 2025.

title: Convivio × Kalio
about: A brand launch documentary made for Convivio in partnership with Kalio. It follows Daniela and her brother, fourth-generation chefs from Abruzzo, Italy, as they bring their family's table to Byron Bay: a long-awaited collaboration built on consistency, care and the belief that gathering around food is the deepest connection we have. Convivio is Latin for coming together around the table, and the film captures one evening at a Kalio residence where exceptional food, wine and conversation let people be fully present. A portrait of family, place and the kind of hospitality that keeps drawing people back.
approach: We sat each person from Convivio and Kalio down for an interview, drawing out Convivio's story through Daniela and Atilio, then captured the event itself as it unfolded across the evening. It was a pleasure to learn the family's history first-hand and to film a night that felt genuinely warm and alive, letting the conversations and the moments at the table lead the edit.
impact: The film supported Convivio's brand and business launch, introducing Daniela, Atilio and their family's story to a wider audience right as they opened their doors. Shot at one of the beautiful properties Kalio manages, it also showcased the kind of setting and experience that defines both brands, giving each a piece they could carry forward.
description: Brand launch documentary for Convivio, hosted by Kalio. Cinematic brand film produced by Bryant Atelier, a Byron Bay video production studio.

title: Bytropic Nutrition
about: A commercial brand film for Bytropic Nutrition, made to anchor a campaign across social media, a hero film and website visuals. Built around the Byron Bay lifestyle, it places the product inside the everyday rhythm of the coast: the kitchen, the car, the surf and the water.
approach: Pre-production followed by two shoots across two days. The first was an indoor day for the kitchen scenes and product close-ups; the second was a beach day for the car, surfing and underwater scenes. Throughout, we worked closely with the talent to capture the ideal Byron Bay lifestyle the product lives in.
impact: Two days of filming gave Bytropic a versatile library of assets from a single production: a hero film, cut-downs for the social media campaign and stills and visuals for the website. One cohesive look, ready to carry the brand across every channel.
description: Brand film for Bytropic Nutrition by Bryant Atelier, a Byron Bay cinematic film studio. Brand films for health, wellness and lifestyle brands across Australia.

title: Koud × The Breath Haus
about: An event documentary capturing a three-day retreat hosted by Koud and The Breath Haus at the Bunker House in Byron Bay. Koud invited thirty strangers from across the country to live together under one roof, built around connection and wellness: ice baths from Koud and breathwork sessions from The Breath Haus. After months of preparation, what unfolded was three days of genuine connection, where a house full of strangers became a community.
approach: Filmed solo as a single-person crew across all three days, documenting the whole event from start to finish. The aim was to never miss a single unique moment, capturing everything from B-roll of the retreat to micro-interviews with every person involved, so the final film could hold the full arc of those three days.
impact: Made for Koud's brand launch, the film puts community at the centre of the brand rather than product. It carries forward the feeling of those three days, the strangers who became friends and the connection the retreat created, giving Koud and The Breath Haus a lasting piece that shows what they stand for.
description: Event documentary capturing the Koud x The Breath Haus retreat. Cinematic film by Bryant Atelier, a Byron Bay video production studio working with wellness and retreat operators.

title: Rogue Watches
about: A feature piece for the Rogue Silver Dive Professional watch. The aim was to create something that invoked a sense of wonder while showing that the watch is built to be submerged, carrying it through different locations and water.
approach: Shot with a single crew and the help of a first AC. The focus was on experimenting with macro work, shooting tight, up-close sequences with the watch submerged in water. It was an exciting piece to make and a chance to push what macro can do underwater.
impact: The result is a product hero piece that lets the Silver Dive Professional speak through detail and atmosphere, proving its submersibility while carrying a real sense of wonder. The macro and underwater work gives Rogue a distinctive, cinematic way to show the watch off.
description: Rogue Watches brand film by Bryant Atelier, a Byron Bay video production studio. Cinematic brand films for premium product and lifestyle brands.

title: Craved This
about: A cinematic brand film for Craved This, a brand bringing chocolate and connection back to ritual through their intimate couples aphrodisiac. One of three parts of a brand launch campaign, it is built around a single scene of love and affection set in a quiet farm field in the Byron Bay hinterland, distilling the essence of the brand into a feeling rather than a pitch: warm, intimate and timeless.
approach: It began with storyboarding, shaping a single scene that would carry the brand's feeling of love and affection. Shot with a small, intentional team, just myself on camera and the Craved This talent, in a quiet field in the Byron Bay hinterland. Keeping the crew lean kept everything focused on the emotion, the talent and the light.
impact: As one of three videos in the launch, the film helped Craved This introduce itself with a clear, emotive identity from day one. Beyond the campaign edits, the shoot also produced website visuals and assets the brand can keep using, made to stay timeless rather than tied to a single moment.
description: Craved This: a cinematic brand film produced by Bryant Atelier, Byron Bay. Brand films for soulful operators across the Northern Rivers and worldwide.

title: Good Old Days
about: A spec project made for fun with friends, built around the idea of the good old days and looking back on good times shared together. A short, timeless piece carried by a classic Ford truck with a look all its own.
approach: A relaxed crew with a few shooters, out to capture timeless moments around the Ford. We played with a range of shots and plenty of drive-bys, leaning into the truck's character and the feeling of the era.
impact: One of our earlier pieces, this was really a hint at our practising of storytelling and visual sequences. A low-pressure project with friends that helped sharpen the craft we now bring to client work.
description: Good Old Days: a Lineage Films Original, made in Byron Bay. A short, timeless spec film carried by a classic Ford truck.
